accepted_units.title: A cocycle transports multiplication while preserving associativity, unit, and classical limit
accepted_units.why_material: The twist is constrained by three semantically distinct requirements: the two-cocycle law supplies associativity, counit normalization preserves the unit, and the formal zeroth-order condition recovers the undeformed structure. Composing the original product with the inverse twist then transports an algebra into a coherent deformed algebra.
accepted_units.context_note: The twist formalism is established mathematical background, here specialized to vector fields and functions. This unit records the general transport mechanism and does not treat the physical interpretation of the deformation parameter as evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Correctness depends on the precise tensor action, using the inverse twist, formal-power-series completion, and exact cocycle and normalization identities; normalized Sweedler indices, bars, and superscripts require source verification.

accepted_units.title: Twisting the coproduct creates a triangular structure whose R-matrix controls interchange
accepted_units.why_material: Conjugating the coproduct and antipode transports the Hopf structure, while the derived universal R-matrix relates the coproduct to its opposite and supplies coherent reorderings. This isolates noncommutativity in a reusable compatibility object rather than treating reordering as arbitrary.
accepted_units.context_note: The Hopf-algebra verification and triangular identities are standard or cited and partly deferred to an appendix. No novelty relative to the corpus is inferred.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The construction depends on invertibility, the exact antipode conjugator, cocycle identities, tensor-leg conventions, and the triangular rather than merely quasitriangular condition; formula-level reuse needs the preserved typeset source.

accepted_units.title: Deform an algebra and its symmetry action together to retain compatibility
accepted_units.why_material: The same underlying vector space becomes a module algebra for the twisted Hopf algebra only when its product and the coproduct-governed action are transported coherently. The proof shows that associativity, equivariance, and the unit each descend from a corresponding twist axiom.
accepted_units.context_note: This is presented as a basic theorem about twisted representations, not a physics-specific result. The displayed proof is algebraic and exact in intent, though indices are damaged in normalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The action, product, coproduct, and tensor convention form one package; deforming only one component would not preserve the module-algebra law.

accepted_units.title: Replace antisymmetry and Jacobi by R-controlled braided versions
accepted_units.why_material: A deformed commutator closes on the original space of generators when the ordinary swap is replaced by the R-matrix action. Antisymmetry and Jacobi survive in braided form, showing how an algebraic law can be transported by modifying its symmetry constraint rather than copying the classical formula unchanged.
accepted_units.context_note: Closure and the braided identities are algebraic claims; the Jacobi proof is repeated in the appendix. The unit does not assert that every noncommutative bracket arises from such a triangular twist.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The exact bracket, ordering, R versus inverse-R convention, and graded or tensor indices are essential and are moderately corrupted in normalized text.

accepted_units.title: Choose between isomorphic presentations by the structure needed downstream
accepted_units.why_material: Two deformed Hopf-algebra presentations are shown isomorphic, yet one has a coproduct whose second tensor factor remains a vector field and therefore supports the intended differential calculus. The example demonstrates that abstract equivalence does not make representations equally convenient for a construction.
accepted_units.context_note: The isomorphism is cited to related work and expressed through a formal map. The downstream choice is mathematical engineering within the deformation framework, not evidence for the paper's gravity model.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The preference depends specifically on coproduct shape and closure properties; exact maps, inverse maps, tensor factors, and R-matrix notation need typeset verification.

accepted_units.title: Transport tensor multiplication and covariance as one associative module-algebra structure
accepted_units.why_material: Applying the same twist prescription to tensors yields an associative deformed tensor product, a braided rule for moving functions past tensors, and a compatible symmetry action with a deformed Leibniz law. This is a systematic extension from scalars to composite objects.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction assumes the standard tensor-field module and a finite local trivialization result cited in a footnote. It does not independently validate any physical interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Tensor order, the module base algebra, R-controlled exchange, and coproduct convention are constitutive; normalization damage makes exact component formulas unsafe.

accepted_units.title: Deform the wedge while retaining the exterior differential through commutation with the action
accepted_units.why_material: The form module and exterior algebra are transported with the twist, producing braided antisymmetry, while the exterior derivative itself remains undeformed because it commutes with the Lie action. The unit distinguishes which operations must change from which can remain fixed under a representation change.
accepted_units.context_note: Local component decompositions and the unchanged differential are standard or cited consequences of the twist setup. No claim is made beyond this class of deformations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Grading, wedge order, antisymmetrizer, and commutation of the differential with the action are required; damaged degree and R-index notation must be checked.

accepted_units.title: Transport a pairing and reconstruct dual frames by enforcing module linearity
accepted_units.why_material: The pairing between vectors and covectors is deformed with the same twist and constrained by covariance and left/right module linearity. A formally invertible pairing matrix then repairs a classical frame into a deformed dual frame, and linear maps are identified with covectors through the pairing.
accepted_units.context_note: The recursive matrix inverse is a formal construction, not a numerical algorithm or convergence claim. The equivalence with left-linear maps is attributed to related work.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Left versus right linearity, pairing orientation, formal invertibility, and the chosen frame matter; overbars, indices, and inverse-star notation are damaged.

accepted_units.title: Define a covariant derivative by linearity and a coproduct-compatible Leibniz rule
accepted_units.why_material: The covariant derivative is fixed by additivity, module linearity in its direction, and an R-controlled Leibniz rule in its argument; compatibility with contraction then extends it to covectors and all tensor types. This shows how coherence constraints propagate an operator from generators to composite objects.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is formal and coordinate-independent in intent, with local coefficients only a representation. It is not an empirical or physical claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. The particular coproduct, left module convention, R-controlled term order, dual frame, and pairing compatibility are essential; exact local formulas need source verification.

accepted_units.title: Use braided symmetry and module linearity to make torsion and curvature tensorial
accepted_units.why_material: Classical torsion and curvature formulas are modified by R-controlled exchange, then tested for braided antisymmetry and left module linearity. Tensoriality is therefore not assumed from notation: it is the criterion that selects well-defined deformed objects from otherwise ambiguous orderings.
accepted_units.context_note: The full technical proof of linearity is cited; the source provides an explanatory reordering argument. The result is internal to the triangular twist framework.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Ordering, R versus inverse-R, the braided bracket, the covariant-derivative rule, and module side determine whether cancellation and linearity hold.

accepted_units.title: Rebuild cyclic symmetry with a braided transposition before stating Bianchi
accepted_units.why_material: A transposition operator compatible with both bimodule and symmetry actions replaces ordinary swaps; its composites define braided cyclic permutation. Under vanishing torsion, the curvature then satisfies a Bianchi identity whose cancellation uses braided Jacobi and Yang-Baxter coherence.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a formal identity under a torsion-free assumption, not a generic identity for all noncommutative connections. The proof is condensed and formula-heavy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high. The cyclic operator, tensor-leg order, Yang-Baxter equation, triangular identities, and R-index conventions are indispensable and visibly damaged in normalized text.

accepted_units.title: Define contraction only after proving frame independence and module linearity
accepted_units.why_material: The Ricci object is formed through a specifically oriented deformed pairing, then checked to be independent of the chosen dual frame and left module-linear. This turns an apparently familiar index contraction into a well-defined invariant rather than an ordering-dependent expression.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is algebraic and uses the previously established tensorial curvature and pairing correspondence. It does not establish physical adequacy of a resulting field equation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Pairing orientation, dual-frame convention, contraction order, and left/right module laws matter; normalized indices are unsafe for exact component reuse.

accepted_units.title: Define symmetry and nondegeneracy through transported transposition and inverse pairings
accepted_units.why_material: The deformed transposition is compared with classical transposition on the shared vector space, allowing symmetric tensors to be transported. Nondegeneracy is expressed by two inverse pairing equations rather than by silently commuting matrix entries, and the classical inverse is recovered at zeroth order.
accepted_units.context_note: The claim that many metrics remain compatible is a mathematical observation within the framework. The subsequent Einstein equation is excluded as model-specific physics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High. Symmetry uses the chosen braided transposition, inverse conditions depend on pairing orientation and product order, and formal zeroth-order nondegeneracy does not by itself imply analytic convergence.

accepted_units.title: An extra twist condition transports conjugation into a compatible real form
accepted_units.why_material: The source does not assume that the undeformed involution automatically survives: it imposes a compatibility condition on the twist, derives antimultiplicativity for products and brackets, transports conjugation to tensors and pairings, and expresses metric reality and inverse relations in a dual basis.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a conditional real-structure construction. Reality of the mathematical tensors does not independently validate the physical gravity equation mentioned nearby.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high. Antipode, flip, complex conjugation, sign, product order, paired basis, barred indices, and star inverse are all essential and several are damaged in normalization.

Novelty and duplication relative to the frozen parent corpus were not inspected and remain unconfirmed.
